subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should `openclaw status --deep` positively surface live gateway memory runtime/provider health for plugin-owned memory when embedding readiness is skipped, or should the current `not checked` wording remain the intended status contract?
rationale: Current main deliberately avoids the old false `unavailable` wording, while the linked fork PR and reporters expect a stronger `gateway active`/provider signal; that is a user-facing diagnostics contract choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Adopt live-runtime status
options.body: Rework the linked idea on current main so status/JSON can show live gateway memory runtime/provider health separately from embedding readiness, with tests and no local plugin side effects.

options.title: Keep not-checked contract
options.body: Close or redirect the linked fork PR and leave this issue open only if reporters can show a remaining misleading status message under current documented behavior.

options.title: Track broader work only
options.body: Move the remaining design to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 if maintainers want one canonical issue for local status probes versus live gateway truth.

recommendation.title: Adopt live-runtime status
recommendation.body: Rework the linked idea on current main so status/JSON can show live gateway memory runtime/provider health separately from embedding readiness, with tests and no local plugin side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the user-facing CLI/status diagnostics contract, and steipete has recent history on the shared status scan surface.
